Catalog gaps (in the bulletin but not in public/courses.json, left out): LX 327, 368, 369, 372, 374, 376, 381, 386, 490, LG 315, LS 504, PH 486.

Sub-250 list first (bulletin numeric order) with cap 1; a second sub-250 course stays unclaimed here and can count in group 5. children.label: One additional course
children.note: Or another related course with advisor approval (use ⋯ → Substitute a course).
children.devNote: Bulletin group 5. A plain COUNT placed after groups 3 and 4: siblings claim left to right, so those fill first and only leftovers count here (no REMAINDER/totalRequired to keep in sync). The first list is the union of the group 3 and 4 lists; group 3's 'at most one below LX 250' cap is per-group, so a second sub-250 course can count here. NE 544 / PS 544 are the same dual-listed course (both keys exist); listing both is harmless since min is 1. PH 486 is in the bulletin but not in public/courses.json, left out.

children.label: Four language courses
children.subtitle: Third-term level or above, two different non-native languages
children.note: Counts language courses at the third-term level or above from Romance Studies, World Languages & Literatures, Classical Studies, or American Sign Language. Study-abroad courses: use ⋯ → Substitute a course.
children.devNote: Bulletin group 6. Subjects from the bulletin department pages, prefixes checked in public/courses.json: Romance Studies = LF, LI, LP, LS; WLL = LY (Arabic), LC, LG, LH, LN (Hindi-Urdu), LJ, LK, LZ (Persian), LR, LT; Classical Studies = CL (Latin/Greek only, explicit list since CL is mostly civ) + CG (Modern Greek; WLL page refers it to Classical Studies); ASL = SED DE. Every language's third term is numbered 211 in the catalog, so min 200 works; no third-term course is below 200 (LF 113, LS 123, LI 131/132, LY 139, LH 139, LC 116, LK 116 are first-year/intensive/heritage). Max 599 keeps out 6xx graduate courses (Reading X for Graduate Students, workshops). Excludes: 200-599 courses whose catalog title says 'in English' / 'in English translation' / 'taught in English', plus ones whose exact title matches an English-taught cross-listing (XL, CL, HI, EN or RN: LI 330, LY 441, LC 227/260/261, LG 235/388, LN 260, LJ 260/261/282/388/460, LK 260/261, LR 327, LT 388/389). Display: one entry per language (label = language name); the first entry of each department carries `heading` and the rest use continues, so each department is one box of collapsed language rows. Latin/Greek lists leave out directed study (CL 493, 494, 497, 498). ASL list = ASL 3 and up (383-386, 583-586, 590-592); DE 472/534/672 (ASL structure, linguistics) and DE 693 (graduate) left out. African languages (LA, LD, LE, LM, LO, LW), LL and LX not included: not on the three department pages. E-suffixed keys never match a range. Group 4/5 courses in these subjects (LJ 410, LJ 510) are claimed by those nodes first, so nothing is counted twice. The two-languages rule is the sibling ling-ba-two-languages (UNRESOLVED).

children.label: Two different languages
children.note: Your four courses must cover at least two different non-native languages. This isn't checked automatically.
children.devNote: Bulletin group 6: 'covering at least two different non-native languages'. The engine can't count distinct subjects within a node.

children.label: Charles River Campus
children.note: At least 6 of your 12 major courses need to be taken on the Charles River Campus. This isn't checked automatically.
children.devNote: Bulletin residency rule. Study-abroad (E-suffixed) courses are kept out of every list.
